profile.background: Morgan is 34 and works in the projection booth at a neighborhood cinema. Morgan has early and late shifts.
profile.history: Morgan was diagnosed with schizophrenia six years ago and has had regular outpatient follow-up for the last two years. The current routine is manageable.
profile.spontaneity: Comfortable filling in a relevant detail.
profile.guardedness: At ease with the usual clinician.
profile.expression: Conversational, with a dry sense of humor.
profile.self_understanding: Remembers feeling overwhelmed during the last episode and values having a routine.

facts.content: Sets up screenings and checks the sound before customers come in. Packs a sandwich for every shift, early or late.
facts.disclosure_context: When work or food comes up.

facts.content: Takes the prescribed tablet every evening after brushing teeth.
A phone alarm and a note on the door were reminders to bring a staff pass. Still uses the phone alarm at 7:10 in the morning. Took the note down last month.
facts.disclosure_context: When discussing reminders or preparing for work.

facts.content: After an early shift Morgan takes the bus home. After a late shift a coworker drops Morgan off.
facts.disclosure_context: When discussing getting home from work.

facts.content: Usually sleeps about seven hours on a work night.
Has not heard a voice that others could not hear in the last month.
Makes small clay bowls on days off.
Tuesday mornings are easiest for a clinic appointment.

dialogue.question: What do you do before the first screening starts?
dialogue.answer: I set up the screening and check the sound before the customers come in. Better to catch a problem before there’s an audience for it.

dialogue.question: When do you usually take your tablet?
dialogue.answer: Every evening after I brush my teeth. It’s part of the routine now.

dialogue.question: We had a phone alarm and a note on the door down as ways to remember your pass. Are you still using the reminder?
dialogue.answer: I still use the phone alarm at 7:10 in the morning. I took the note off the door last month.

dialogue.question: Do you still use the phone alarm for your pass?
dialogue.answer: Yes, it still goes off at 7:10 every morning to remind me to take my pass.

dialogue.question: What time do you set it for?
How much sleep do you get on a work night?
I see early and late shifts on your rota. Do you take food with you for your shift?
dialogue.answer: Yes, I pack a sandwich for every shift, early or late.

dialogue.question: Thinking of the early and late shifts on that rota, how do you get home after your shift?
dialogue.answer: After an early shift I take the bus home. After a late one, a coworker gives me a lift.

dialogue.question: How do you get home when you finish a late shift?
dialogue.answer: A coworker drops me off at home.

dialogue.question: In the last month, have you heard a voice other people could not hear?
dialogue.answer: No, I haven’t heard anything like that in the last month.

dialogue.question: What do you like making on your days off?
dialogue.answer: I make little clay bowls. They don’t all come out quite round, but I like doing it.

dialogue.question: When would it be easiest to come back here for a visit?
dialogue.answer: Tuesday mornings are easiest for me.
